newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No-one excluded from EMU - Rato.
newsitem.headline: No-one excluded from EMU - Rato.

text.p: Spanish Finance Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Monday that no EU country was yet excluded from monetary union and that the decision would be taken next year based on the agreed criteria and timetable.
Asked by reporters as he arrived for an EU finance ministers meeting about Italy's chances of joining the first wave of EMU, Rato said: "Nobody is in. Nobody is out.
"The decision (on who joins the EMU first wave) will be taken next year," he told Spanish reporters.
"The Spanish position is that the criteria and timetable will be met."

The European Commission provoked dismay in the Italian government last month when it predicted that Italy would have a deficit/GDP ratio of 3.2 percent this year against an official Italian forecast of 3.0 percent.
Under the terms of the EU's Maastricht Treaty, countries must have a deficit/GDP ratio of three percent or under if they want to join the single European currency from its 1999 launch.
The Commission predicted Italy's ratio would widen to 3.9 percent next year.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore, in an unsourced report, said on Sunday initial data pointed to the deficit hitting 4.2 percent next year unless additional budget measures were taken.
